title: Multi-Asset Funds: Simplifying Your Investment Portfolio
description: Multi-Asset Funds are mutual fund schemes that invest in at least three different asset classes, with a minimum of 10% allocation to each. They aim to provide.

faq.q: Are Multi-Asset Funds suitable for beginners?
faq.a: Yes, Multi-Asset Funds can be a good starting point for beginners. They offer diversification and professional management, simplifying the investment process and reducing the need for active portfolio monitoring.

faq.q: What is the minimum investment required for Multi-Asset Funds?
faq.a: The minimum investment for Multi-Asset Funds, like most mutual funds, can vary. Many funds allow SIPs (Systematic Investment Plans) starting from as low as ₹500 per month, making them accessible to a wide range of investors.

faq.q: How do Multi-Asset Funds differ from balanced advantage funds?
faq.a: While both diversify across assets, Balanced Advantage Funds (also known as Dynamic Asset Allocation Funds) dynamically shift between equity and debt based on market valuations or predefined models, often without a minimum 10% allocation to three distinct asset classes. Multi-Asset Funds, by SEBI definition, must maintain at least 10% in each of three asset classes.

faq.q: Can I invest in Multi-Asset Funds for short-term goals?
faq.a: Generally, Multi-Asset Funds are best suited for long-term goals (5 years or more). While they aim to reduce volatility, short-term market fluctuations can still impact returns, making them less ideal for goals with a horizon of less than 3 years.

faq.q: How do I choose the best Multi-Asset Fund?
faq.a: Consider factors like the fund's historical performance (over 5+ years), expense ratio, the fund manager's experience, the fund house's reputation, and how its asset allocation strategy aligns with your risk tolerance and goals.

faq.q: Do Multi-Asset Funds invest directly in real estate?
faq.a: Typically, Multi-Asset Funds do not invest directly in physical real estate. Any exposure to real estate is usually indirect, through investments in Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) or equity shares of companies operating in the real estate sector.

faq.q: What are the tax implications if I sell Multi-Asset Fund units within a year?
faq.a: If the fund has 65% or more equity exposure, gains are taxed as Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) at 15%. If it has less than 65% equity exposure, gains (for units purchased on or after April 1, 2023) are added to your income and taxed at your income slab rate.
